Prologue   The end of the first age of mankind happened in the late part of the 21 st  century. Without fanfare mankind was erased from the planet but a most unlikely source. During an expedition in Antarctica a  relice  was found, this relic advanced mankind by decades giving birth to a new host of technology and abilities. It was not until three decades later that the objects true purpose was discovered, despite multiple attempts to destroy or remove it from the planet it kept returning. In the last decade before the inevitable, a new plan was hatched, a desperate plan, with the device five alien’s in cry statis pods had also been found. After much investigation it was theorized that no human could survive cryogenic  sleep,  until one such scientist found the answer, by combining a biological component found within the alien species to a human they could successfully freeze and then restore them.   Five years to the day of the destruction of man, those volunteers were sent out into the deep vastness of space where they slept for two centuries. The ships built with a powerful Artificial intelligence returned the pods to earth. Those who landed found no trace of humanity or its monuments. Left to  there own  devices they created a new society, a new world.  The second age of mankind was born, but an unexpected side effect had occurred, those that  returned,  those that had been altered in order to survive developed strange  abilities,  sharing a relationship with a  mysterious crystal structure that had invaded every region of the world.  Some of these sleepers never returned, left to sleep in the darkness of space due to a miscalculation one by one they returned over time, to a world they didn’t recognize or a planet that no longer resembled the one they left.  This is the story of one such sleeper… ONE M A R C U S.     It is said that only those who have felt pain understand what it means to truly be alive, in that moment of awakening Marcus experienced an epiphany of existence through the lesson of pain, more pain then one man should be able to endure he thought in between the waves of debilitating agony wracking his newly awakened body. For four centuries he had slept, his body hanging in a delicate balance between life and death, now reawakened his mind fought for control of a brain that had not processed a thought in all that time synapse fired as paths not used for centuries began to repave themselves causing waves of emotion and random images to shoot through his mind without context or meaning. There was no concept of self, no concept of human only of pain and of light, so much light his mind thought as his eyes remained closed pain assaulting the retinae’s that had not been subject to oxygen much less vision in those four centuries , blind and barely functioning he lay there for what seemed like an eternity trying to remember who he was and why he was there eventually, slowly his body began to respond to stimuli.   Running his trembling hands over his arms they came away covered in a clear slimy film of  chemicals and condensation, he tried to shift in the small space he occupied, the action almost impossible in the tiny capsule, claustrophobia began to well up as he felt blind panic begin to overwhelm his already taxed system, it took him many minutes but finally he was able to calm himself. Eventually he gave the command for his arm to move but it remained unresponsive, taking a long slow breath he soothed down another tidal wave of panic as it tried to crash over his mind, and with a sigh he tried again and a small smile of victory spread across his face as he felt the muscles quivering in response.  Summoning what little strength he had Marcus once again sent the command MOVE he thought as the muscles continued to quiver under the strain of the simple order, finally, slowly his arm moved unsteadily upward fighting gravity as it ascended above his body reaching out and clumsily grabbed the metal lip of the pod.  When you wake, your body will take time to recover as your brain relearns to receive input from your senses and nerves, this will be true for your muscles as well, despite being frozen there is a part of your subconscious we believe is still aware on some level and will require some time to reacquaint itself with the body  he heard a voice somewhere from deep within his addled mind. There had been a briefing he remembered one where they told him the infusion of alien DNA would keep the most basic part of his brain alive and working despite his body being frozen, something about needing that in order to revive the  body then came the questions as his mind desperately tried to reassert itself, tried to reconnect with its identity,  who had told him? ,  where had he been?  Before he could follow that train of thought the memory and the impending self-realization descended into the thick fog that seemed to hover over his consciousness. He lay there for what seemed like days as his mind slowly cleared the fog beginning to dissipate, not thawing he thought reawakening, that was the term the scientist had used he recalled as his synapses learned once again to fire after a millennia of deep cold sleep. Words came to him as he continued to lay there  don’t panic ,  give your body time to recover  came a calm voice from long ago, Marcus controlled his breathing keeping the panic at bay as it continued to threaten to take over.  Eventually his muscles began to respond to his commands, slowly he regained control of his hand. The simple manual dexterity required to work the small panel at the edge of his blurred vision nearly impossible as it took him eight tries before he first recalled and then was able to punch in the sequence that released the canopy and retracted the harness holding him in place. Exhaustion and trauma took over his body as darkness closed in on his vision descending his body and mind into unconsciousness and mercifully Marcus slept a sleep filled with random images, sounds and thoughts. Sometime later he awoke his still blurry vision able to tell only that it was now dark as Marcus began to test his limbs once again.  They responded though erratic at first and Marcus was reminded of a newborn fowl as it took its erratic first steps and smiled at the thought  you have been sleeping for centuries man, relax your body is going to take time to work again  he reminded himself. concentrating, he did his best to cut through the fog that threatened to once again overtake him and forced his body to move, pushing up, his head cleared the canopy and he let out a primal scream, unleashing the pain and frustration pushing it out through his vocal cords until he went hoarse as the last of his breath expelled, he fought against another bout of blackness as it edged into his vision but to no avail as his body once again descended into blackness.  The next time he awoke he could see the beginnings of daylight, his vision improving and his muscles surer, more responsive.  Specialist Marcus Gavin  he reminded himself as his identity and reason for being there finally resolved in the muddy pit that his mind had become.  Army  he thought  I am in the army, was in the army  his mind corrected as the events leading up to his being stored in the cryopod began to come back to him.  Unsteadily he pulled himself over the lip and fell the ten feet to the soft moss-covered earth below the pod, his nose was filled with the smell of plants and decaying wood as he  lie  there, face down once again on terra firma for the first time in an eon.  An eternity later he was able to stand, his mind and body recovering as the sun lazily traveled higher into the sky beams of sunlight dancing through the tall forest canopy, as he looked around finally regarding his surroundings.  Marcus surveyed the dense forest and thick lush green plants as the smell of Aspen and Cottonwood carried over a light cool breeze that managed to snake its way through the tall forest around him, the familiar scene calming him but still something wasn’t right, something he was supposed to see but didn’t and it took him a few moments to pull the thought from the rats nest of information that was his newly reawaken mind  pods  he thought,  I should see and hear the landing of the other pods of other volunteers  he reminded himself as more of the briefing he had received prior to entering stasis came  back to him.  Recalling again the voice of the unknown scientist whose face floated as if just under the surface of a lake, the features blurry as the words played through his head  You will land in groups, four centuries from now once we are sure that the danger has passed, each pod is fitted with a beacon so if you find yourself alone or in a small group, use it to find others and gather, there is safety in numbers and from there you will be able to coordinate and prepare to move out either to the bunkers of supplies that have been left or with those that come to rescue you if we have survived  the words faded in his mind giving him an empty feeling as he surveyed his surroundings and seeing no sign of either humans or landed craft.  Marcus felt the frustration as he was unable to hold onto the thought as it just submerged itself into the noise that was his mind. He forced himself up on unsteady legs, feeling the bite of the old gnarled trunk against his palm as he leaned against it using the old wood to help him stand, his body once again his own he looked out over the subdued reds and yellow colors of the leaves in the unfamiliar forest ,  its fall, fall here in the northwest  he thought. Looking around realizing he was very much alone, and finally feeling something other than pain as fear washed over him as the quiet rustling of branches and the soft calls of animals emanating from somewhere deep within the woods his only companions.  Walking around the oblong metal craft that had been his home nestled in the larger ship that still circled the earth he surveyed the minor damage to the hull and the path of destruction that led its now final resting spot. It took him a few moments to work the small ladder out of the side allowing him to easily traverse up over the lip of the cockpit, he saw the red fabric of the statis bed, wires and tubes lay in a mess as they had been ripped off of and out of him the memory of his thrashing and bucking as his body had once again regained consciousness, this nest of tubes and needs a reminder of where he had been these past four centuries. Hanging onto the edge of the pod, he located the small number pad, after four attempts to finally enter in the code, which helpfully had been scrawled above the keypad in permanent ink, had he done that? Marcus wondered regarding the scribble and trying  to recall what his own handwriting looked like. A light tone came from the pod as it accepted the code and for a moment nothing happened, Marcus was about to enter it in a second time when the stasis bed slid forward revealing a packed storage compartment behind it. Reaching in, he pulled out the large black pelican cases and tossed them over the edge of the pod listening as they each made a satisfying thump onto the ground below.  Ensuring he had gotten everything Marcus slowly and unsteadily made his way back down the small ladder to the forest floor the exertion leaving him short of breath and then for the first time he noticed his breath, the white vapor pushing out of his mouth, smiling as the memory of falls past began to surface in his head his body however, mercifully still too numb to feel the cold but that did not mean he was impervious to it and he quickly set about finding something warm to wear . Opening the cases one by one he began to survey the equipment, to his relief he found the small GPS unit and turning it on breathed a sigh of relief as the bright green screen lit up revealing a spinning hourglass and the word loading as it started up, setting it aside he began to pull other items he would need from the cases, breaking the shrink-wrap seals he rummaged further in the case, a smile of relief broke across his face as he spied the two packs of shrink wrapped coyote-tan battle dress uniforms, jackets, gloves and 5.11 tactical boots.  He stripped off the black gortex unibody outfit still covered with the now drying chemicals and quickly got dressed in the dry clothing, using one of the spare t-shirts to wipe off the excess chemicals and moisture off of his body,  not a hot shower  he thought, but it would have to do.  Once he was dressed he felt less exposed his mind and body were feeling almost to their old self, Standing up he stretched the long limbs on his six foot two inch frame feeling the ample muscles still present from his years of service as a specialist in the Army Military Police he felt a pang of regret that his career in the military, though brief had come to an end, but he had volunteered for this project, understood what it would mean to the human race and quickly squashed his fear and regrets, he was here now, on earth and if all had gone well humanity had survived he reflected. He was not bothered by the peaceful look of the planet despite the warnings of what would happen once the machine had activated, he knew the scientists had calculated enough time to ensure that the event was over and the planet would heal before humans would return to the planet. Digging into the first pack he found the Ontario K-Bar knife and survival hatchet which he clipped on his belt and then smiled again as he reached in and picked up the military m-4 carbine and m-9 service pistol. With an expert hand he checked the rifle, picking up one of the clips he slapped it in hearing the reassuring metal clang as it seated into rifle,  pulling the charging handle he loaded a round into the chamber. Looking around he found the biggest tree he could taking careful aim he squeezed the trigger and was rewarded with a dry click, curiously he looked at the weapon and pulled the charging handle again , expending the round and loading a new one he aimed pulled the trigger and another dry click, he tried it ten more times, then switched magazines and tried it again every time getting the quiet click. “Shit” he whispered pulling the magazine and grabbing a few rounds looking down at his hand he studied them, but they looked normal he thought could it be possible they gave him bad rounds he wondered. Pulling the pistol and trying that as well he squeezed the trigger getting only the dry click, he pulled the receiver and loaded a new round. “Fucking great” he spat putting the weapons back in the pelican case. Was it possible the cordite went bad he wondered, or had they just given him shitty rounds? Well hopefully that wouldn’t matter he thought as he looked to the sky hoping to see a spotter plane or helicopter and was quickly disappointed as the only thing that ruled the blue and pink morning sky were the large birds lazily flying overhead.  Marcus reached down to pick up the little electronic screen and saw that it now displayed a menu, he carefully looked over the icons until he found the one that looked like a radio  antennae . Touching it with his finger it displayed a generic map screen as a progress bar began to step forward. He waited impatiently as the little device tried to connect with other pods or bunkers or  Search and  resue . Again that calm baritone voice of the Scientist spoke in his head  Every Pod is fitted with a beacon, when you land use your TIMS device to find your fellow ARC members, your TIMS unit also has the ability to transmit so that you will be able to guide yourself to either other members or there pods. Now there will be bunkers laid out, buried to ensure that if you return and the worse has happened, you will have every resource you need to rebuild society. Find the bunkers, find your fellow ARC members. This is your first priority  the voice said, fading into memory as he watched the small bar continue to march across the screen. Finally, it completed, and Marcus stood there for a moment staring in disbelief at the small screen as the small box with the simple phrase continued to blink up at him. “No signals in range” it stated simply, and he just stared at it  how is this possible  he wondered,  even if there had been no pods , he should have found a satellite or transmission signal or hell even a broadcast, the planet   was lousy with them   was being the operative word he surmised as the pang of fear began to manifest itself, growing and tightening in his gut. “No, this isn’t right” he whispered shaking his head, Marcus exited the locator screen and went into settings, he quickly found the small icon for diagnostics and clicked it, another loading bar displaying as it happily announced, “Checking Unit”. After a moment it dinged and Marcus looked down, staring at the small screen as a chill passed over his body. ‘Unit working, range 2000  Km, errant signals detected: 0’. The fear grew in his stomach, not a signal or satellite could be found, nothing on the planet broadcasted. Looking out at the large forest Marcus felt very much alone.  After a few moments he turned off the unit and after a moment of looking himself over he, dropped it into one of the cargo pockets that ran down his leg, he began to gather the gear spread out before him.  If there is no signal here, then we will have to go somewhere, where there is one . He thought but in the back of his mind he wondered if it was possible that earth had not survived, that the ARC project had not survived, and he was the last person left on the planet. He quickly dismissed it because if that were true then he was good and fucked he thought digging through the boxes and collecting various items out of the black plastic cases. Well at least I have the knife and hatchet he thought pulling a coyote-tan pack over to him. Unzipping it he began rummaging through the contents until he produced a black digital radio, on the side it had a simple hand crank allowing you to charge the radio, he cycled the crank for a good five minutes stopping a few times to shake out his hand as the repetition of the action was causing his long dormant muscles to cramp. He flipped the power button and was rewarded as the digital display glowed bright green showing it was set to shortwave and displaying a series of numbers. Marcus looked over the simple controls and finally hitting the scan button he extended the two antennae, maybe the TIMS unit was malfunctioning  and didn’t know it he thought staring hopefully at the screen of the small radio.  He sat there hunched over the radio as the numbers cycled three times, four times then after ten the green display dimmed. “Dammit” he whispered cranking the radio again until the display brightened. Marcus looked to the sky Well maybe  its  too clear to get a signal, no clouds, no bounce he thought remembering his simple training on the radio, shortwave signals can travel great distances bouncing off of the atmosphere repeatedly. He checked the settings and found the one marked “weather” switching the setting he was yet again rewarded with nothing, not even electronic interference, there was just nothing. He sat there allowing the radio to die, cranking it back to full power and then repeating the cycle again and again as he sat there for two hours desperately listening for any sign of civilization.  This doesn’t mean anything it just means I am too far into the woods to get a good signal  he thought putting the radio back in the bag and rummaging through the contents again until he came out with a book of maps, a package of rations and a compass.  He studied the maps for several minutes while sucking on the silver package of what was supposed to be peas, aside from the undesirable green color it tasted more like dirt he thought, wincing as he sucked at the tube again. With no coordinates, GPS or decent landmarks to orient the map it was next to useless, so he put it back, seeing the canteen attached to the molle hooks on the outside of the  bag he grabbed it and realized it was empty.  I need to find water  he thought  which means I need higher ground if I want to find out where the hell to go so, I can get back to civilization, I can do this   confidence in there being a civilization to get back to was eroding fast.  Packing the bag and zipping it up he hefted it , testing its weight then with a nod of approval ,  strapped  it to his back  moving his back and checking the weight against the straps . After a few moments  of deliberation  he took the pistol and rifle, returning it to the pod’s cargo compartment , looking at the small box containing the weapons he resolved himself that until he had ammunition the items were merely dead weight,   closing the secure door, watching as the mechanism engaged  allowing the seat to settled back into position  hiding the cargo compartment from all except those who were familiar with the pods .   Randomly choosing north Marcus began to walk  through the thick underbrush, spying the  half  empty branches of the trees and bushe s  he judged it to be late autumn or early winter . “Well it could be much worse, you could be  trecking  through three feet of snow there Gavin” he said smiling at his use of his last name  bringing back the recent memories of his time in the army .  In the back of his mind he still couldn’t shake the fear,  twenty  thousand people should be landing or landed  based on the briefing they should be doing it around the same damn area he  thought. As the sun  climbed  further into the sky Marcus walked carefully navigating the woods and brush, he could hear the lazy calls of the animals and the smell of  of  the forest  heavy in the  air,   he took in the ambience of the woods, his eyes always searching for people or evidence of pods and seeing none .  Walking  through the forest, he began to notice odd crystalline growths along the ground and on the trees , more  then   few as almost every tree, rock and even the ground itself had evidence red, green and even black crystal spires growing over everything, almost like an invasive species had been introduced to the  environment,  kneeling close to one such growth he studied it for a moment “What the hell” he said reaching out and touching the deep red crystal spire .  Marcus quickly pulled his hand away looking curiously at first the crystal then his  hand  as he slowly reached out again and touched the smooth crystal  surface . He felt a vibration within the small spire similar to the feeling of touching a power transformer it was like feeling large amounts of current flowing through the small stone. Marcus cocked his head studying it for a moment and then looking out across the expanse of the dense forest he could see growths as far as the eye could see on almost everything. “What the hell happened?” he asked himself as he stood continuing to walk as his eyes kept finding the crystals on everything from trees to bushes to rocks.  This was evidence of something, something beyond his familiar world , the more he moved north,  the  more his eyes searched out and found the spires and growths emitting from everything . Marcus had grown up in the suburbs and aside from the army had spent very little time In the woods, except for some training missions he thought and never had he seen crystal formations growing all around  so does that mean this is something new, or something that happened because of the event or hell, is it just  Im  in the crystal forests of nowhere  montana  he wondered wryly.  Making his way north he kept expecting to come across a road or an old cabin or some sign of humans and the longer he went without seeing  it,  the more worried he became . The need to find any sign of civilization  becoming  more desperate with every step. He couldn’t be alone; it was impossible he told himself but the further he walked the less sure he was  as  the forest seemed to stretch on forever.  Walking over a small hill a breeze  rose , blowing through the trees and rustling the brush. Closing his eyes he tilted his head towards the wind allowing it to  pickup  his blonde hair as he felt it lightly caress his cheeks the feeling calming him as if the feeling somehow awakened some primal feeling of warmth and love as if the hand of his mother were stroking his face. His eyes shot opened as he breathed in the  cold  air moving through the winds and the smell of mint filled his nose.  As a child he remembered playing by an old creek along the shore grew the small mint plants, the smell bringing back the memory of that which he  needed more  then  even other people, water. He followed the direction of the breeze, catching the heady smell of the small plant here and there on the wind. Finally, the forest opened up revealing a small creek. Marcus smiled as he pulled out the canteen from the outside of the pack. On the  surface  of the cover of the old military surplus item was a pocket, from it he pulled a small blue tablet, filling the canteen he dropped the tablet in closing the bottle and shaking it well allowing the purification tablet to do its work before opening the bottle and greedily upending the canteen.  He refilled it twice, both times ensuring to use the little tablets. He drank until he felt he would burst and finally sated with drink, he filled it one last time and attached it to his belt where it would be easily reachable, right next to the knife. Marcus walked north again until the sun began to wane bringing dusk to the forest.  He had found no sign of humans , he was desperate  he was so desperate to prove his fears wrong, at  one point he had thought he had caught sight of a deer stand, stumbling through the brush at nearly a run he had come upon the tree to see that it was only a fallen branch that hung in a way to look like a crossbar.  He had not seen any sign that anyone had come through this forest no trash, tracks or tell-tale signs of hunters. As dusk settled over the forest he found a small clearing,  pulling   a  small tent from the pack he erected the pole fragments into supports and then running them through the loops he quickly had the small blue dome erected he unrolled the small sleeping  bag  that had been attached  underneath the pack  pulling  out the waterproof matches from a side pocket. It took him nearly thirty minutes to collect enough wood to build a decent fire.  It had not rained in at least a week so the wood along the forest floor was decently dry and he thanked his good fortune, the pack only had a limited amount of kindling and he wanted to use it sparingly. An hour late as darkness had finally come to the forest and the nocturnal calls of the animals began Marcus sat there with the radio trying in vain to hear anything along the channels that would confirm he was not alone. Eventually  exhaustion  overtook  him,  and he gave up, crawling into the tent  undressing Marcus  neatly  laid  out his clothes for the next day  lying down he looked into the darkness and said a small prayer for his species .  H e lay there trying not to think about what he would do if he found no sign of the others. Instead he thought about his friends from the project, for two years he had trained and gone through treatment after treatment of infusion and gene therapy, the doctors inserting a tube in one artery, pumping his blood into a machine that would infuse his blood with a green substance , something they said would allow him to be able to be revived from Cryogenic Sleep and then the blood, now altered on a genetic level was pumped back into his body.  He was forced to do this almost daily for months until they were able to confirm his body had taken to the process. The doctors seemed pleased at his  body’s ability to accept the substance and adapt to it. During his time there he had met a few people but of them only three had become friends. Gabrielle Ramirez, Joe Marconi and  Bethany  Smith. They had been like the four musketeers he thought smiling at memories of the four of them as they heatedly debated anything. He remembered the day they sat, stunned after a month of entering the top-secret project they had been told that humanity would end, and they would resurrect it. That was a heavy weight on all their shoulders but leaning on each other had made the news bearable he  recalled . He drifted off to sleep with thoughts of his friends and slept with nightmares of being alone on earth. Marcus awoke as the sun began to light the outside of the small tent;  laying  there watching as the shadows of the trees played across the fabric like an old Chinese puppet show. Eventually he got up and dressed.  It took him no time at all to disassemble the small tent and secure everything back to the pack, sitting there with the smoldering pile of ash that only the night before had been a pillar of firelight that kept the darkness at bay he sucked at another silver tube, this one said squash but again wincing as he took another helping from the  silver  tube and tasting the bitter chalk taste. Before setting off Marcus pulled all of the tubes from the pack and lining them up on the ground and accounting for rationing of two tubes a day, he had enough food two weeks he thought. He needed to find civilization or a lake  where he could fish  otherwise,  he was going to have to learn to hunt with a spear  he thought.  He had gone through the army survival courses, knew how to hunt and dress an animal to eat, but training and doing were two very different things he surmised sighing heavily at the scant supplies. He packed up the food, taking only two mouthfuls from the canteen he set out again heading north. Putting one foot in front of the other he made his way through the forest and along game trails, always on the lookout for any sign he was approaching people. It wasn’t until  mid day  that he his luck appeared to change. Marcus walked along the small path that from the tracks looked as if deer frequented it.  Maybe it will lead to water  he thought as he  carefully followed  the well-worn path.  Making  his way down the  game trail , something caught his eye the small or medium sparkling of the crystals that still covered every tree, rock and even the ground had become so common place he didn’t even notice it anymore, but something had glinted, not glass or crystal but metal he thought moving past a few trees as he searched the distance for whatever it was that had caught his eye. Then in an instant it happened again, Marcus catching the sight of something silver in the brush, he broke out in an excited sweat  people  his mind screamed and he broke out into a run .  Abandoning his normally safe pace, he sprinted across the woods hurdling brush and fallen trees with no thought to what lay on the other side. He did not take his eyes off of the small view of that silver surface as he sprinted for all he was worth.  Coming to the  marred steel side  he pulled back the bush that covered it, ripping it away trying to uncover the one sign of mankind that he had seen since landing.  Afer  a moment he had pulled away nearly all the brush to reveal another pod. He stood there his chest heaving at the effort as he realized that  this  pod had sunken partway into the ground  its discolored surface spoke to exposure to the elements, long exposure his rational mind said . Marcus leaned in and his heart fell as he came face to face with the mummified body of the occupant.  “ Fuck ”  he whispered collapsing  against the old relic  and  sliding down the side of the stained metal to sit in the dirt.  Almost  he thought as tears stained his cheeks,  his mind tried to understand what this meant, was it someone who landed early and died, did everyone land and this man had died on impact and they left him here, were  they  the only two people left his mind raced trying to make sense of the find , getting up  he began to   check   over  the occupant.  Marcus could see easily what had happened and now he understood why it was buried, the chute had not deployed examining the bottom of the pod he could see the entire underside was crushed from the impact.  Whoever this was had died still in  cryo  he thought looking  at  the  dessicated  form of the only other human he had seen.  But where there is one, there are others  he thought  a small kernel of hope sprouting in his mind, others had landed he thought, others might have survived  his mind continued latching onto the train of reason that would allow him to push forward and continue  searching .  He spent almost an hour trying to get into the cargo area of the pod, but it was too damaged,  the keypad had been crushed and any power had long ago  run  out,  he had no tools to cut it open. After a time, he abandoned it, not wanting to leave a working gun if one had been in there, but his lack of tools giving him little choice.  Sliding down the side of the old relic Marcus sat there staring out over the forest “Have you seen anyone else, have any others come to see your grave?” he asked the corpse as he  slumped,  defeated against the side of the pod.  He needed a plan, needed a destination he thought and then an idea began to form into his mind as he looked to his left and saw water  peaking  through the trees. Slowly getting up he followed the sound and glinting blue reflection until he stood on a bank, the river was large and as he surveyed the surface, he could see a bend and a fork. Reaching into his pocket he pulled out the TIMS device, turning it on he waited impatiently for the device to turn on. One of the random pieces of information he remembered about the device was that prior to launch, it would download the latest maps and pictures of the globe, allowing him to have accurate maps even after all this time. The device chimed as the main menu displayed.  Marcus swiped the screen until he came to what he was looking for. Pulling up a real time picture of the area he had supposedly landed he searched until he found the river and then slowly tracing  it,   found what looked like the right bend and fork.  Using the menu  options,  he superimposed the location of bunkers and just about slapped his forehead, he was close, in fact according to this, he had passed one already.  “You are such a dumbass” he whispered thinking of the food and supplies that would be available and more  importantly,  weapons and far superior com equipment. He had been so focused on finding people that his mind had abandoned him.  He followed the paths, found the landmarks and quickly found himself within a kilometer of a bunker , his heart beat with excitement at the thought of the gear and the equipment that he could use to ascertain the location of his fellow volunteers and the supplies that would be available to him.  He sped up his pace quickly making the time to the small dot on the map.  Marcus ascended the final ridge  stepping over the large vines and other plants that attempted to hinder his progress as he moved with a purpose,  his hopes soaring as he came over the top and stopped,  standing  there  he  quietly  reguarded  the  large hole that was supposed to be a  four-story  bunker that descended into the earth. “What the fuck” he said tears coming to his eyes as all hope  crumbled  from his heart. “What the holy fuck” he screamed at the top of his lungs as the words echoed off of the crumbling  dirt  walls of the surrounding hole.  In its place a large garden of blue and green crystals reached into the sky the concentration was far greater  then  anything he had seen since landing, it seemed as if the crystals  themselves had replaced the bunker and all its contents . Where had the bunker  gone?  had they even finished  it,  or had they been interrupted? His mind raced trying to resolve the question.  Trying to keep the panic down he reviewed the map and by that night he sat by a fire staring into the distance, four more bunker locations visited, and all had been the same as the first, a hole filled with crystal. No sign that a bunker had even existed.  As if all evidence of construction or even the building  itself gone , just gone as if they had never existed. Upon viewing the collection of weapons, Marcus could see they still had a long way to go before they would reach the technology level he had left, but the resin, repeating  rifles and rotary cannons  were a hell of a start he thought .  The Silvan’s had  grown and created   a  crystal slug creating something that even in his time was not yet freely available rounds that didn’t require a shell to fire,  they had discovered the ability to grow slugs that were two different crystal hybrids and by piercing them both, created an explosion sending the majority of the shell out towards the enemy with the power of a magnum round .  He had carefully examined the  weapons,  the smooth bores told of the path they still had yet to travel,  but the deviation from his own technological timeline spoke of some powerful weapons he reflected .  “General, I have to ask I thank your people for helping those of the  lowlands,  but you mentioned something about other races” Marcus queried, the way the General had used the term bothered him. He had seen the changes done to these people, genetics altered with the use of science and magic had created something akin to a new race, one closer with the forest he thought. The General studied the trees as  Silvans  leapt from branch to branch, staying behind trunks in an effort to spy on the camp at the bottom of the hill.    He was quiet for a long time as Marcus  reguarded  the large oval eyes and then he turned to face the Mage “There are others, changed by the first ones who live further to the north, however they keep to themselves, we stopped trying to talk to them ages ago, our people live on the border and even our  interaction with those of the low lands have been limited. “People fear what they do not understand Master Mage, you  will do  well to remember that” he said his eyes hovering to the open collar of Marcus’s shirt where the blue pulsing runes were visible.  He  self consciously  closed the jacket buttoning it up to his neck and turned back to the forest.  “ Whats  next General?” Marcus asked and the other man’s face spread back into a predatory smile. “Well Master Mage, the enemy will meet our battle riders” he said and the young Mage cocked his head “I didn’t think you owned horses” he said and  Durass  chuckled “We don’t Master Mage, we don’t” he said turning and walking into the house, Leaving Marcus to stand alone on the porch.  Looking down at the camp his hand unconsciously went to his waist and rested loosely on the curved blade attached there, the runes glimmering off the silver blade as sunlight played down the metal.  The voices in his head were quiet, they had been for a while but the knowledge was still there, but the same way your body would get used to a foreign object in it his mind had adapted to the knowledge, he could access it , but it no longer overwhelmed him he thought still staring at the fires in the distance.  Even with the vast amount of knowledge in his mind he still didn’t know how to defeat the Queen’s guard and the Seers with  there  creatures, they would  come,  and he would fight but Marcus did not know if it would be enough.  He knew there had been two Seer’s in the  came , had sensed them and now more had come, along with more of the  creatures they commanded, reaching out with his mind he closed his eyes, allowing his will to play over the forest as he felt  ten  seer’s and over eighty of the creatures in the  came .  They had called everything here, pulled the Seers and creatures from the towns he reflected to fight here. What was so damn important that the Queen would need to ensure overwhelming force. Then he remembered the Black runes across Rogan’s body, his black eyes and the comments from the Ancient Sylvan mage, she had done it wrong. Did the queen need to find the proper mixture or find the process for ensuring that adapting the runic magic to a mage worked  properly?  He thought about it, what was the  concequenses  for not doing it correctly he  wondered,  and no answer came as it so often did these days.  The knowledge he possessed didn’t have that answer he marveled.  He felt like a man out of time, his love was gone, his friend might even now be dead. Dara had left and Patrice was busy with the wounded, that was all he had in the world he thought a few friends and the memory of someone he loved more  then  life itself.  Marcus knew he would  fight;  knew he would defend this strange race of people as his mind wandered over the memories of children playing and young couples lounging in the park. These people did not deserve the fate that came for them, but that wasn’t why Marcus would fight, that is not why tomorrow morning he would descend the elevator and put himself between the enemy and this city. It was simply because it was the  Queen’s people who had  take  Orah from him, she did not deserve to win, did not deserve to succeed he thought turning from the forest and entering the house.  That night he dreamt of Orah, of the Queen and the darkness a darkness that called from beyond the sea, something is coming the shadowy visage of the queen said as she stood among the black rocks of the beach and pointed out towards the ocean. A low thrum echoed from the ocean’s horizon, sounding a little closer each time it sounded. Orah’s arm snaked over his as his love leaned in close “Its evil Marcus, it is death that comes across the ocean” she said. Turning he looked into the eyes of the woman who had been his world. “Orah,  Im  sorry, I  could’nt  save you” he whispered, smiling she opened her mouth to speak and to Marcus’s horror flame erupted, setting her on fire “Save them Marcus, watch the oceans, it comes for the power” her voice whispered as fire engulfed her.  He sat bold upright in bed and for a moment he searched the room for the flaming body of Orah realizing he was in the General’s guest room. A sound was echoing from the  window,  then reality descended onto him as he shot out of bed, He had no idea how long the alarm had been going off, but it  could’nt  be good he thought. Throwing on his clothes, he grabbed the weapons and bolted from the room. The General was in the main foyer preparing to leave when he turned to see the Mage rushing down the stairs. Marcus could see the worried look on his face “They are marching up the  hill, more of the Seers and creatures are present and they used kinetic force to destroy the rotary cannons.” He said turning to the door with Marcus on his heels.  “We have one more line of defense before we have to retreat to the city itself and prepare for a siege” the General said.  Marcus stopped him putting a hand on the man’s shoulders “General, if they take the land before the city needs to be abandoned, the mages will throw fire until this entire city is engulfed, I think I know what they want and the condition of the city doesn’t matter” he said the General looked at the Mage and Marcus could see the stubborn determination in his eyes “We will not give up the city mage” he said turning and brushing Marcus’s hand off his shoulder. They rode the elevator down in silence both lost in thought of the coming battle.  As it reached the bottom  Durass  stepped out and took a long silver horn from one of his soldiers. “You are going to want to see this Master Mage” he simply said and smiled as he raised the horn and blew a long note that resounded through the area, echoing off the trees.  All was quiet for a moment and then a  cacauphony  of growls erupted from the other side of the field and everyone turned. Marcus’s jaw dropped as Silvan warriors erupted from the bushes on white  bangel  tigers the size of small cars. The creatures were massive the riders looking almost tiny on the massive creatures. Saddles and reigns had been strapped onto them and they bounded across the large  field,  more growls erupting from the beasts.  Marcus noticed the belts wrapped around the riders and couldn’t understand why they were tied into the saddle until the first of the creatures leapt against a tree and began to climb into the branches above. “That’s amazing” he breathed watching as it reached a large branch, bounded over it and launched itself into another tree and then another, finally directly above the  army,  the beast dropped into the battle.  Twenty of the cats descended into the middle of the enemy and began to tear apart soldier after soldier.  He had never seen anything like it.  Leaning forward he watched as the cats dominated the field as the riders pulled long curved swords, what the cats couldn’t get the riders did as bone and steel lashed out spilling blood and bone over the forest floor. For a moment Marcus hoped that they would win, that these animals and the surprise attack would win the day, but these soldiers were not inexperienced, they were well trained and battle hardened, and quickly moved into a defensive position locking in the animals as they held them off with spears and swords.  Marcus felt it before he saw it as the ten robed seers walked into the crowd of soldiers, moving them with power as they walked in a line towards the trapped animals. Some of the large cats had managed to leap over the soldiers retreating further up the hill, but eight of them still stood  there  ground, hissing, growing and slapping at the long steel tipped spears. The animals kept trying to move forward, angered by the weapons and then the Seers stood there, like the horsemen of the  apocalypse ,  a line of black robed monks with the cowls raised showing only a shadow where there faces should be. Marcus’s eyes widened “get them out of there  Durass ” he said but it was too late, three of the Seer’s extended out hands and Marcus felt as the power roiled through them three of the animals exploding into flame as beast and man screamed and thrashed. “NO” Marcus screamed and with and thrust kinetic energy at his feet he launched into the air and sailed over the crowd of soldiers as they stood shocked at the sight of the engulfed and screaming animals.  Sailing over the crowd, he pushed out with his power steadying his body as he arced in the air, the power in his runes running like water over his body as he came careening down towards the ground he pushed out once again with kinetic force, slowing himself and landing lightly on his feet. Now he stood before the Ten Chosen of the Queen another had pulled power and launched it towards another rider and his beast. Marcus flicked his hand in a  well practiced  motion that came from within the repository of knowledge in his mind and the energy  richocetd  and a tree burst into flames nearby.  “That’s enough” he said standing stalwart between the chosen and the  Silvan’s.   There would be no more death he vowed looking over the black robed Lords of the Queen’s court.  “This is finished Mages, there will be no more death upon this field unless  its  yours” he stated, his voice even as he delivered the threat.  Eyeing the  line,  he fought back the nagging fear that whispered in the back of his mind. What the hell  was I thinking he chastised  himself,  he knew he could beat one, he had fought Rogan, knew what he was capable  of,  but ten of them. Marcus didn’t know if he had the power to fight all of them.  The soldiers surrounding the group had gone quiet as the fighting stopped, everyone now focusing on the group of Mages standing in the center of the field facing each other.  A laugh floated from the line and one stepped forward pulling back his cowl as Marcus recognized the face of Rogan, his obsidian eyes seemed to light with enjoyment as he took a few more steps and then stopping  reguarded  Marcus as he shook his head.  “We have been here before Marcus, but I didn’t expect you would be so willing to walk into my clutches after last time, but it seems as if you wish to be delivered to my Queen after all” he said shaking his head.  Marcus took a breath anger overtaking the nagging fear as he watched the self  righteious  asshole strut like a peacock up and down the line. “This stops here Rogan, how many have you killed, how many have you destroyed in the name of power” Marcus shot accusingly at the other man.  Rogan stopped cocking his head and looking at Marcus “You defend these” he said waiving a hand at the soldiers surrounding him. “They are  mundanes , they are meant to serve us Marcus, we are the powerful, the chosen. The queen has a plan and the Mages will save the world, we will unite all people under our power and lead them to salvation. Surely you understand this” he said almost astonished that the other man would place  himself in the same sentence with those who weren’t mages.  But Marcus didn’t like bullies, he liked entitled pricks less “That’s your problem Rogan, you actually think your better  then  them, you think for some reason that because you have a gift, instead of using it to benefit those around you, you instead think you should control them” Marcus observed and Rogan again looked confused “Of course we are, we are the strong , they are the weak. It is the natural order” he said as if the reason were  self evident .  Marcus shook his head and laughed but there was no humor in the sound “How many people have you killed to fuel your grab for power Rogan, you think your original , you really think you are the first people to do this, to rationalize this. Hell Rogan,  its  so common it’s a fucking cliché” he spat.  “You make me sick, so here is the deal, surrender and I will let you live” Marcus stated.  For a moment the field was quiet, no one moved as everyone looked on in amazement as the small group continued to face off. Then Rogan threw his head back and laughed, Marcus could hear chuckles from the other Seer’s as well. Hell at least he was entertaining he  thought,  his stomach sinking as he realized, he was going to have to fight these men.  Marcus did not think he would live, but maybe, just maybe he could hold them off long enough for  Durass  to come up with a plan to save the city, when he lost, they would turn  their   attention to those above him and the city would burn.  A vision of  Orah,  burning in bed as he burst into the room shot through his head and the anger overtook all fear pushing it out, leaving only the cold fire of vengeance heating his soul.  With a resigned sigh he reached  down,  pulling the small black staff from his side and holding it loosely he began to pour power into the object, feeling the runes along the hilt heat in response.  If he was going to die, he would take as many as he could with  him  he thought tensing  as he felt the power coursing through his runes and over his body   as, for the first time in centuries a Runic Mage prepared for battle .  The benefit of being able to see the flow of power became evident a moment later as he watched the two Mages on either end change as  their  runes began to glow power gathering and doubling as they pulled power to them.  Without warning hands shot out and kinetic force flew from either side trying to catch Marcus off guard. But he had been prepared and with a flip of his wrist the staff  extended,  and he pulled it up flipping it over his hand and catching the kinetic strikes with the runes on the hilt. The energy absorbed by the staff.  Catching the staff as it finished its  rotation,  he pushed out his other hand and extended the staff towards the mage on the left, releasing the energy along with some of his own. He watched as the bolt of kinetic force slammed into the man, catching him in the chest and throwing him back into a line of trees. Cracking sounds erupted from his body as he  hit the tree and what sounded like a wet smack resounded as his body hit the ground. The mage did not stand and for a moment no one said anything everyone frozen  still,  still looking to where the Mage, one of the Queen’s chosen had just been killed.  Rogan turned his head locking his eyes on Marcus and he could see the anger behind those black eyes as the man’s face twisted in rage “You will pay for that Mage” he spit.  Rogan whistled and the nine remaining mages pulled  there  own  staves, some splitting them revealing the dual blades, others extending it like a  wand,  the entire group’s weapons now trained on Marcus as he stood there waiting for the attack that would end his life.  Rogan moved first as Marcus watched the mage collect energy, he pushed kinetic force into the ground below him, launching himself into the air, he split the small stave in two, flipping it so the hilt ends pointed at Marcus. As he reached the pinnacle of his arch gouts of flame shot from the end of the staves Marcus knocking it away without even a thought, he prepared for the mage to land.  As Rogan’s feat touched the ground, Marcus collapsed his own stave, splitting it and holding it out daggers first.  Rogan rushed forward, throwing hit after hit and then a jet of flame and then a kinetic strike, the sticks moved with such speed, enhanced by his magic as he struck again and again but Marcus had the muscle memory and training of generations of mages and matched him blow for blow, knocking  back strikes and parry magic the two stood there facing off as the hilts and blades clashed against each other, magic spitting off the weapons in arcs of flame and  electricy .  As he matched Rogan’s  strikes,  he felt the energy behind him as three of the Seers threw bolts of  electicity  at him. Marcus without even a thought threw down a kinetic blast careening him left and out of the way of the blasts. Rogan did the same the two mages crashing into a surprised group of soldiers who until that moment had been  stunned,  watching the two.  Rogan drew power, picking up Soldiers and throwing them at Marcus who quickly batted them out of the  way,  he moved towards his opponent.  Rogan began to circle  him,  and Marcus responded, keeping the mage in front of him and then he stopped smiling “You have gotten stronger” he said and Marcus was about to respond when he felt the force of the remaining seers wrap around him., Kinetic energy snaking around his body like snakes as the energy  tightented . Rogan still smiling relaxed his stance. “Oh, I don’t want you dead Marcus, our Queen has plans for you” he said standing there as energy continued to wrap Marcus  into a  kinetic  cacoon .  No,  he thought, he couldn’t let this happen. He wouldn’t allow the Queen to get ahold of him, he had no idea what she had planned but he knew it  would’nt  be good. Rogan turned his back on the young mage and looked up at the city as he conjured a small gout of flame in his palm as he continued to look up.  Marcus looked to the flame, the memory of Orah still hung in his mind “No”  Marcus whispered the power holding him in place, crushing the air out of him, he could no longer breath as blackness began to edge into his vision. “no” he said again as the Runic Mage began to gather power, the runes pulsing as he pulled more and more energy into himself.  Closing his eyes he felt the kinetic vines of power seeing the power course over him, poking at the snakes of power his eyes snapped open as he felt the hollow centers of the spell and as a predatory smile spread across his face he launched all the accumulated energy into the vines of power breaking in through the outer shell his power shot back like water in a pipe and all at once the eight Mages were thrown off there feat and launched backward as the power exploded into them. The vines of power  disintegrated,  and Marcus was suddenly free. He had no time to pull more power, Rogan had started to turn so Marcus pushed the end of one of the staves towards him, expending the stored power within it, the Mage caught by surprise was thrown forward into a tree.  No more he thought turning to face the eight mages, one no longer moving the other seven stood shakily.  Marcus stalked forward “No More” he yelled, pulling power as he felt the runes heating his skin as he continued to expend his gift. He thrust the blades towards two of the Black Robed figures as lances of fire shot into them , the two seers erupting into fire, no time to defend themselves and then flicking his finger he threw another kinetic strike at the next Seer, he quickly batted it away, but that had been a distraction as he threw one of the blades at the mage, putting  magical force behind it , it sped like a bullet impaling the mage into the tree behind him.  He saw the kinetic blast as the next seer summoned it and before he could throw  it,  Marcus summoned electricity and lighting erupted from his fingers playing over the mage just as he began to try and throw the strike. He stood for a moment his body jerking as the electricity struck him over and over, finally Marcus let  go,  the Mages body falling to the ground.  At that moment Marcus finally understood what it meant to be a Runic Mage, he no longer had to pull energy, no longer had to stop and recharge, he felt the energy coursing over his body, using the runes like a canal his runes pulling energy itself allowing him to keep throwing spell after spell the power coursing from his fingers was almost godlike he thought as he reached up pulling one of the larges trees out of the ground with magical force and slamming it  ontop  of the remaining Seers.  He slowly turned to face a now unsteady Rogan, standing there with blood trickling down his face the Seer stood his ground. “I am the queen’s  chosen;  I am all powerful, you will not best me Mage” he spat as Marcus  reguarded  him silently.  Reaching back with his hand Marcus summoned the staff blade and it came flying to his hand, he reassembled the small weapon, his eyes still not leaving  Rogan’s.   “Surrender” Marcus stepping towards the Queen’s chosen. Rogan smiled and then his hand moved in a blur throwing lightning of his own before  marcus  could react it hit his chest and was absorbed by his runes. Both men stood  there astounded “What are you?” Rogan breathed his eyes wide now as he stared at the other man.  “Your executioner” he said and with a wave of his shot a pillar of fire at the other Mage, the flame so hot the Mage’s scream only lasted for a moment before his body began to disintegrate.  “Surrender or Die” Marcus yelled to the field as the soldiers stood there astounded.  Marcus now saw the Screamers retreating in the distance, they never even came to the Seer’s aid he thought shaking his head. Soldiers began to lay down  there  weapons and put  there  hands up as Wardens and Silvan’s secured prisoners as the battle for the city in the trees ended.
